questions.question: You’re late for a meeting with your boss, and they’re already in the conference room. What is the most appropriate way to apologise?
options: I’m sorry I’m late. I’ll try to make it up to you later.
Sorry, I’m running behind. See you soon!
I’m sorry I’m late. I’ll bring coffee next time to make up for it.
I’m sorry I’m late. It’s not my fault.
questions.answer: I’m sorry I’m late. I’ll try to make it up to you later.

questions.question: Your friend says, *'I think we should move to London for the summer job.'* How would you politely suggest an alternative?
options: No, that’s a terrible idea. We should stay here.
That’s a good idea, but what if we try Manchester instead?
London is too expensive. I suggest we don’t go at all.
I’m not sure, but maybe we should ask your boss first.
questions.answer: That’s a good idea, but what if we try Manchester instead?

questions.question: Your colleague says, *'I don’t think this project will finish on time.'* How would you respond if you disagree?
options: That’s a great point! We should start immediately.
I disagree—we can definitely meet the deadline if we work harder.
I think you’re wrong; we’ll finish it soon enough.
I see your concern, but I think we should focus on other tasks.
questions.answer: I disagree—we can definitely meet the deadline if we work harder.

questions.question: You’re helping a student with their homework, and they ask, *'Can you explain this part again?'* What is the best way to respond?
options: Of course! Let me show you step by step.
No, I don’t think I can help with that.
You’re welcome! Here’s the answer—just take notes.
Sure, but only if you promise to finish the rest by yourself.
questions.answer: Of course! Let me show you step by step.

questions.question: In a formal business email to a new client, you want to express your opinion about their product. Which sentence would you use?
options: I really like how you’ve designed this product—it’s very innovative!
I’m not sure if this will work for our needs, but I’ll let you know.
Your product is okay, but it doesn’t match our brand’s style.
I think you should improve the packaging before releasing it.
questions.answer: I really like how you’ve designed this product—it’s very innovative!
